stem: Which two factors together express a risk level?
explanation: A risk is characterized by its likelihood (probability of occurring) and its impact (the harm if it does). Together they express the risk level.

stem: In test-driven development, what happens right after a new test is written?
explanation: In TDD the test is written first, then code is written to satisfy it, and then both are refactored.
options: Code is written to pass it
The test joins the CI pipeline

stem:
Which single test achieves 100% statement coverage of this code?

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{READ a}\\\texttt{READ b}\\\texttt{IF a > b THEN}\\\texttt{\ \ PRINT a}\\\texttt{ENDIF}\\\texttt{PRINT b}\end{array}$$
explanation: Only a test where a is greater than b executes PRINT a inside the IF. With a = 5 and b = 2 every statement runs; the other tests skip that statement.

stem: A team has run the same regression suite unchanged for two years, and it no longer finds new defects. Which principle explains this?
explanation: Tests that are repeated many times become less effective at finding new defects, so tests and test data need updating. Exhaustive testing being impossible is about scope, not repetition.

stem: Why do black-box test cases stay useful when the implementation changes but the required behaviour does not?
explanation: Black-box techniques are based on the specified behaviour without reference to internal structure, so the test cases are independent of how the software is implemented.
options: They test only the user interface
They do not depend on the code

stem: Which review role mediates, manages time and keeps the meeting safe for everyone to speak?
explanation: The moderator (facilitator) ensures review meetings run effectively, including mediation, time management and a safe environment. The review leader organizes the review overall.

stem: For a testing task, experts give most optimistic 4, most likely 10 and most pessimistic 22 person-days. Using E = (a + 4m + b) / 6, what is the estimate in person-days?
explanation: E = (4 + 4 x 10 + 22) / 6 = 66 / 6 = 11 person-days. 12 is the plain average of the three figures and 10 is just the most likely value.

stem: Which test activity answers the question "how to test?"
explanation: Test design elaborates test conditions into test cases and other testware, answering how to test. Test analysis answers what to test.

stem: Which is a project risk?
explanation: Project risks concern managing and controlling the project, including supplier issues such as a third party failing or going bankrupt. Wrong calculations, slow responses and security holes are product risks.

stem: Which practice is an example of shift left?
explanation: Shift left means testing earlier in the SDLC, for example reviewing specifications, writing tests before code and running static analysis before dynamic testing.
options: Performance tests left to system test

stem:
What is the minimum number of test cases for 100% branch coverage of this code?

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{IF x > 0 THEN}\\\texttt{\ \ y = 1}\\\texttt{ELSE}\\\texttt{\ \ y = 2}\\\texttt{ENDIF}\\\texttt{IF z > 0 THEN}\\\texttt{\ \ w = 1}\\\texttt{ENDIF}\end{array}$$
explanation: Each decision has a true and a false outcome. One test with x > 0 and z > 0 and another with x <= 0 and z <= 0 cover all four, so 2 tests are enough.

stem: A developer misreads a requirement and codes a 15% discount instead of 5%. At checkout, customers are overcharged. What is the overcharging?
explanation: The misreading is the error (a human mistake), the wrong discount in the code is the defect, and the wrong charge seen when the code runs is the failure.

stem: An order quantity field rejects 0 and negative values. Orders of 1 to 49 get no discount, 50 to 199 get 5% off, and 200 or more get the bulk price. How many equivalence partitions are there?
explanation: There is one invalid partition (0 and below) and three valid ones (1 to 49, 50 to 199, 200 and above), so 4 partitions. A test for each one gives 100% EP coverage.

stem: Which response to a product risk is mitigation by testing?
explanation: Mitigating by testing includes choosing skilled testers, an appropriate level of independence, reviews and static analysis, suitable techniques and coverage, and dynamic testing. Insurance is risk transfer.
options: Accepting the risk as it is

stem: Which review type is led by the author?
explanation: A walkthrough is led by the author and can educate reviewers, build consensus and find anomalies. A technical review is led by a moderator, and in an inspection the author cannot lead.

stem: Which is a typical entry criterion?
explanation: Entry criteria are preconditions for starting, such as available resources and testware and an initial quality level like passed smoke tests. The other three are typical exit criteria.

stem: Testing the interface between a web shop and an external payment provider is which test level?
explanation: System integration testing focuses on the interfaces of the system under test with other systems and external services. Component integration testing covers interfaces between components inside the system.

stem: Which statement about statement and branch coverage is true?
explanation: Branch coverage subsumes statement coverage: 100% branch coverage also gives 100% statement coverage, but not the other way round, because an IF with no ELSE can be fully covered by statements without its false branch.
options: Full statement coverage gives full branch coverage
Branch coverage counts only unconditional branches
They always need the same number of tests
Full branch coverage gives full statement coverage

stem: Dynamic testing triggers a failure. Which activity then reproduces it, diagnoses the defect and removes it?
explanation: Debugging finds, analyzes and eliminates the cause of a failure. Confirmation testing comes afterwards and checks that the fix worked.

stem: During which activity are test procedures arranged into a test execution schedule?
explanation: Test implementation creates the testware needed for execution, organizes test procedures into suites and arranges them in a test execution schedule. It also builds and verifies the test environment.

stem: A temperature setting accepts whole numbers from 10 to 30. Which values give 100% 2-value BVA coverage of the valid partition's boundaries?
explanation: In 2-value BVA each boundary has two coverage items: the boundary value and its closest neighbour in the adjacent partition. That gives 9 and 10 at the lower boundary, 30 and 31 at the upper. The six-value set is 3-value BVA.

stem: Defect density is which kind of test metric?
explanation: Defect metrics include the number and priorities of defects found and fixed, defect density and defect detection percentage. Mean time to failure is a product quality metric.

stem: After a fix, a tester reruns the test that exposed the defect. What is this?
explanation: Confirmation testing checks that the original defect has been fixed. Regression testing checks that the change has not broken anything else.

stem: In session-based exploratory testing, what guides the tester during the time box?
explanation: In session-based testing the tester works within a time box guided by a test charter of test objectives, and the session is usually followed by a debriefing.

stem: Which defect is typically easier to find by static testing than by dynamic testing?
explanation: Static testing finds coding defects such as unreachable or duplicated code and undefined variables. Performance and runtime behaviour need the code to execute.

stem: In the test pyramid, what are the tests in the top layer like?
explanation: Higher layers have lower granularity and isolation and longer execution time. The top holds a few slow end-to-end tests; the bottom holds many small, fast, isolated ones.

stem: Which item belongs in a test progress report?
explanation: Progress reports are produced regularly during testing and include the testing period, progress, impediments, metrics, new risks and the testing planned next. Lessons learned and the final summary go in a completion report.
options: Lessons learned for the next project
Testing planned for the next period

stem: Which description fits quality assurance rather than testing?
explanation: QA is process-oriented and preventive: it improves the processes so that a good product follows. Testing is product-oriented, corrective, and a form of quality control.
options: A major form of quality control

stem:
A shop's shipping rules are shown below. A test uses a non-member whose order total is 60. Which rule does it exercise?

| Condition or action | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Member | T | T | F | F |
| Order over 100 | T | F | T | F |
| Free shipping | X | X | X | |
explanation: A non-member is Member = F, and a total of 60 is Order over 100 = F. Only R4 has F for both, and its expected action is no free shipping.

stem: Which event triggers maintenance testing?
explanation: Maintenance testing is triggered by modifications, upgrades or migrations of the operational environment, and retirement.
options: Adding a new tester to the team

stem: Which item should be left out of a checklist for checklist-based testing?
explanation: Checklists should not hold items that can be checked automatically, items better suited as entry or exit criteria, or items too general. Each item should be checkable on its own.
options: A check that required field labels show

stem: A defect report gives an identifier, a title, the test steps, severity and priority. Which key information is missing?
explanation: A defect report logged in dynamic testing should include the expected and actual results, along with the test object and environment, context, date and author, status and references.

stem: Which work product typically comes from test analysis?
explanation: Test analysis produces prioritized test conditions and defect reports on the test basis. Test procedures and environment items come from implementation, and test logs from execution.

stem: In which review activity is each anomaly given a status, an owner and actions?
explanation: Anomalies are not necessarily defects, so in communication and analysis each is discussed and given a status, ownership and required actions, usually in a review meeting.

stem:
Priority 1 is the highest. In what order should these test cases run?

| Test | Priority | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | none |
| B | 1 | D |
| C | 2 | none |
| D | 4 | none |
explanation: B has the highest priority but depends on D, so D must run first, then B. The rest follow by priority: C (2), then A (3).

stem: Who brings the highest level of independence to testing a component?
explanation: Testers from outside the organization give very high independence. A tester from another team in the same organization gives high independence, a peer gives some, and the author gives none.
options: A peer on the author's team

stem:
A document workflow has these valid transitions. What is the fewest event sequences, each starting in Draft, that give 100% valid transitions coverage?

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| Draft | submit | In review |
| In review | reject | Draft |
| In review | approve | Approved |
| Approved | publish | Published |
explanation: One sequence (one test case) covers all four transitions: submit, reject, submit again, approve, publish. A single test case may, and usually will, cover several transitions.

stem: Checking that a search returns results within two seconds is which test type?
explanation: Response time is performance efficiency, a non-functional quality characteristic: it is about how well the system behaves, not what it does.

stem: In ATDD, which test cases does the team usually write first?
explanation: The first ATDD test cases are typically positive, confirming correct behaviour without errors. Negative testing follows, then non-functional characteristics. Tests should not go beyond the story.
options: Cases that go beyond the story
Negative cases for every error condition

skill: FL-6.2.1 Benefits and risks of automation
stem: Which is a risk of test automation?
explanation: Risks include unrealistic expectations, inaccurate estimates, over-reliance on the tool and dependency on a vendor that may retire the tool or give poor support. The others are benefits.

stem: In a quantitative risk assessment, a risk's likelihood is 0.25 and the impact is 40. What is the risk level?
explanation: In the quantitative approach the risk level is likelihood multiplied by impact: 0.25 x 40 = 10. Dividing instead gives 160.

stem: Which approach expresses desired behaviour as natural-language cases, usually in Given/When/Then format?
explanation: BDD expresses desired behaviour in simple natural language that stakeholders can read, usually Given/When/Then, and the cases are then turned into executable tests.

stem: A component has 40 executable statements. Test A exercises 28 of them and test B exercises 30, with 22 run by both. What statement coverage do A and B give together?
explanation: Together the tests run 28 + 30 - 22 = 36 distinct statements, and 36 / 40 = 90%. Test A alone gives 70% and test B alone 75%.

stem: In operation, most reported failures come from 3 of an application's 40 modules. Which principle does this illustrate?
explanation: A small number of components usually holds most of the defects, an example of the Pareto principle. Predicted and observed clusters feed risk-based testing.
options: Early testing saves time and money

stem: Which category of test technique depends most on the tester's skills and complements the others?
explanation: Experience-based techniques use the tester's knowledge and experience, so their effectiveness depends heavily on skill. They can find defects that black-box and white-box techniques miss.

stem: Which statement is true of an inspection?
explanation: An inspection is the most formal review type and follows the full process. The author cannot act as review leader or scribe, and metrics are collected.
options: The author cannot be the scribe

stem: In past projects the development-to-test effort ratio of 5:2 held steady. Development is now estimated at 750 person-days. What is the estimated test effort in person-days?
explanation: Test effort is 2/5 of development effort: 750 x 2 / 5 = 300 person-days. 1875 comes from inverting the ratio and 214 from dividing by the total of 7 parts.

stem: Ongoing checking of all test activities against the plan is called what?
explanation: Test monitoring checks all test activities and compares actual progress with the plan. Test control takes the actions needed to meet the test objectives.

stem: Which is a product risk?
explanation: Product risks relate to the product's quality characteristics, such as poor response time or wrong functionality. Staff shortages, bad estimates and late environments are project risks.

stem: Which is a testing benefit of DevOps?
explanation: DevOps gives fast feedback on code quality and on whether changes break existing code. Manual testing from the user's point of view is still needed, and the pipeline has to be built and kept up.

stem: What is a weakness of white-box testing?
explanation: If the software does not implement a requirement, white-box testing may not detect the defect of omission. Its strength is that it works even when the specification is vague or outdated.
options: It gives no measure of coverage
It cannot be used at all in static testing

stem: Which is a typical test objective?
explanation: Building confidence in the quality of the test object is a typical test objective. Removing defects is debugging, and testing can never prove that no defects remain.

stem: Payment type has three partitions (card, voucher, cash) and delivery has two (standard, express). What is the minimum number of test cases for Each Choice coverage?
explanation: Each Choice coverage needs every partition of every set exercised at least once, not every combination. Three tests can each use a different payment type while together using both delivery types, so 3 is the minimum.

stem: Which is an example of a test control directive?
explanation: Test control uses monitoring information to give directives such as reprioritizing tests when a risk becomes an issue, adjusting the schedule or adding resources.

skill: FL-3.1.1 Work products for static testing
stem: Which work product is not appropriate for static testing?
explanation: Almost any work product can be statically tested, but not those hard for people to interpret and that should not be analyzed by tools, such as third-party executables for legal reasons.
options: A test charter for a session

stem: Exploratory testing, usability testing and user acceptance testing belong to which testing quadrant?
explanation: Q3 is business facing and critiques the product: exploratory, usability and user acceptance testing, user-oriented and often manual. Q4 holds non-functional tests other than usability.

stem: Who normally performs component testing?
explanation: Component testing is normally done by developers in their development environments, often with test harnesses or unit test frameworks.

stem: Fault attacks are a way of implementing which test technique?
explanation: In a fault attack the tester creates or acquires a list of possible errors, defects and failures and designs tests to expose them. It is a way to implement error guessing.

stem: A retrospective finds that tight deadlines made developers skip input checks, which led to several defects. What are the tight deadlines?
explanation: A root cause is the fundamental reason a problem occurs, such as the situation that leads to an error. Removing it can prevent similar defects. The skipped checks are errors and the resulting faults are defects.

stem: Tracing test results back to risks lets a team evaluate what?
explanation: Traceability of test results to risks can be used to evaluate the level of residual risk in a test object. Traceability of test cases to requirements shows requirements coverage.

stem: A password must be 8 to 20 characters long. Using 3-value BVA on the valid partition's two boundaries, which lengths give 100% coverage?
explanation: In 3-value BVA each boundary value has three coverage items: the value and both neighbours. For 8 that is 7, 8 and 9; for 20 it is 19, 20 and 21. The four-value set is 2-value BVA.

stem: Once a configuration item is approved for testing, what does it become?
explanation: An approved configuration item becomes a baseline and can then be changed only through a formal change control process. It is possible to revert to a previous baseline.

stem: What is advisable before regression testing, to decide how far it should reach?
explanation: An impact analysis shows which parts of the software could be affected by a change, which sets the extent of regression testing.

stem: In INVEST, the criteria for good user stories, what does the E stand for?
explanation: Good user stories are Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small and Testable.

stem: Which is a success factor for reviews?
explanation: Reviewing small chunks keeps reviewers concentrated. Evaluating participants should never be an objective, and reviewers need adequate time to prepare.
options: Reviewing the whole document at once

stem: Which item is typical content of a test plan?
explanation: A test plan typically covers context, assumptions and constraints, stakeholders, communication, the risk register, the test approach, and budget and schedule. Logs and defect reports come from execution.

stem: Which is an objective of a defect report?
explanation: Defect reports give those resolving defects enough information, provide a means of tracking work product quality and give ideas for improving the development and test process.
options: Recording which person caused the defect

stem: Why are communication skills especially important for testers?
explanation: Testers often bring bad news, and test results may be taken as criticism of the product and its author. Communicating defects constructively helps the team accept them.
options: Testers write most of the code
Defect reports must be given verbally

stem: A business rule depends on three Boolean conditions, and one combination is infeasible. How many columns must be exercised for 100% decision table coverage?
explanation: Three Boolean conditions give 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 combinations. Coverage items are the columns with feasible combinations, so 8 - 1 = 7 columns.

stem: Where are the results of a retrospective normally recorded?
explanation: Retrospective results should be recorded and are normally part of the test completion report. Recommended improvements must then be followed up.
options: In the next iteration's test plan

stem: In the 3 C's of a user story, what is the Confirmation?
explanation: The 3 C's are Card (the medium), Conversation (how the software will be used) and Confirmation (the acceptance criteria).
options: The talk about how it is used

stem: A team uses containers so every tester gets an identical environment. Which kind of tool support is this?
explanation: Virtual machines and containerization tools support scalability and deployment standardization. Test management tools handle requirements, tests and defects.

stem: Which activities does the testing role mainly focus on?
explanation: The testing role covers the engineering side: test analysis, design, implementation and execution. The test management role focuses on planning, monitoring, control and completion.

stem: What does early and frequent stakeholder feedback help prevent?
explanation: Frequent stakeholder feedback prevents misunderstandings about requirements and helps changes be understood and implemented earlier, avoiding costly rework.

stem: During iteration planning, what does a tester typically do?
explanation: In iteration planning, testers join detailed risk analysis of stories, judge testability, break stories into tasks (especially testing tasks) and estimate the test effort for them.
options: Write the code for each story

stem: In the whole team approach, who is responsible for quality?
explanation: In the whole team approach any member with the right skills can do any task, and everyone is responsible for quality.

stem:
A pump has three states and three events, shown in this state table (an empty cell is an invalid transition). How many coverage items are there for all transitions coverage?

| State | start | stop | fault |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off | Running | | |
| Running | | Off | Error |
| Error | | Off | |
explanation: All transitions coverage counts every cell of the state table: the 4 valid transitions plus the 5 invalid ones, 3 x 3 = 9. Valid transitions coverage alone would need only the 4.

stem: An application is being retired but its data must be kept for years. What testing may be needed?
explanation: Retirement can require testing of data archiving when long retention is needed, and of restore and retrieval procedures in case the data is needed later.
options: Load testing of the old system

stem: Acceptance criteria written in Given/When/Then form are in which format?
explanation: The two common formats are scenario-oriented, such as the Given/When/Then format used in BDD, and rule-oriented, such as a bullet point verification list or an input-output table.

stem: A distributed team spans several time zones. Which way of communicating test status may suit it best?
explanation: More formal communication may be more appropriate for distributed teams, where face-to-face contact is limited by distance or time differences.

stem: A system passes every test of its specified requirements, yet users reject it as unfit for their work. Which principle applies?
explanation: Testing all specified requirements and fixing all defects can still give a system that does not meet users' needs. Validation is needed as well as verification.
options: Early testing saves time and money

stem: Which task belongs to test completion?
explanation: At test completion, testware that may be useful later is archived or handed over, the environment is shut down to an agreed state and a completion report is written.

stem: In a sequential model such as the V-model, when can dynamic testing usually start?
explanation: In sequential models the executable code is usually created later, so dynamic testing typically cannot start early. Testers join requirement reviews, analysis and design first.

stem: In which review activity are the scope, exit criteria and timeframes defined?
explanation: During planning, the review scope is defined: purpose, work product, quality characteristics, focus areas, exit criteria, supporting information, effort and timeframes.

stem: In equivalence partitioning, what are the coverage items?
explanation: In EP the coverage items are the equivalence partitions, including invalid ones. Boundary values are BVA's coverage items.

stem: Why can 100% statement coverage still miss a division by zero?
explanation: Executing a statement does not detect every defect. A division by zero fails only when the denominator is zero, so it is data dependent.
options: The defect depends on the data

stem: Three-point estimates are optimistic 5, most likely 11 and pessimistic 29 person-hours. Using SD = (b - a) / 6, what is the standard deviation in person-hours?
explanation: SD = (29 - 5) / 6 = 24 / 6 = 4 person-hours. The estimate itself is (5 + 44 + 29) / 6 = 13, so the result is 13 plus or minus 4.

stem: Risk analysis consists of which two activities?
explanation: Risk analysis is risk identification plus risk assessment. Risk control is risk mitigation plus risk monitoring.

stem: After 500 tests pass, a manager announces that the software has no defects. Which principle does this ignore?
explanation: Testing can show that defects are present but cannot prove that there are none. It only lowers the probability that defects remain undiscovered.
options: Early testing saves time and money

stem: Besides finding testable features, what else does test analysis evaluate in the test basis?
explanation: During test analysis, the test basis and test object are also evaluated to identify defects they may contain and to assess their testability.

stem: Which choices do Agile projects usually favour for testing?
explanation: Agile assumes change throughout the project, so lightweight documentation and extensive automation for regression testing are favoured, with manual testing mostly experience-based.
options: Testing only at the end of a release

stem: What is the goal of review initiation?
explanation: Review initiation makes sure everyone is prepared: each participant has access to the work product, understands their role and receives what they need.
options: Everyone has what they need to start
The work product is formally accepted

stem: A tester identifies five equivalence partitions and the tests exercise four of them. What is the EP coverage?
explanation: Coverage is partitions exercised divided by partitions identified: 4 / 5 = 80%.

stem:
What is the minimum number of test cases for 100% branch coverage of this code?

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{IF a > 0 THEN}\\\texttt{\ \ IF b > 0 THEN}\\\texttt{\ \ \ \ x = 1}\\\texttt{\ \ ENDIF}\\\texttt{ENDIF}\end{array}$$
explanation: The outer decision needs a true and a false outcome, and the inner one is reached only when the outer is true. Tests (a > 0, b > 0), (a > 0, b <= 0) and (a <= 0) cover all four outcomes, so 3 are needed.

stem: Testing in the last three iterations took 18, 22 and 26 person-days. Extrapolating with their average, what is the estimate for the next iteration?
explanation: The average of the last three iterations is (18 + 22 + 26) / 3 = 22 person-days. Extrapolation uses early measurements from the current project and suits iterative SDLCs.

stem: What is the aim of risk monitoring?
explanation: Risk monitoring ensures mitigation actions are effective, gathers information to improve risk assessment and identifies emerging risks.
options: Moving the risk to a supplier or insurer

stem: A form has 12 fields, each with hundreds of possible values. What does the syllabus recommend instead of testing every combination?
explanation: Exhaustive testing is not feasible except in trivial cases, so test techniques, test case prioritization and risk-based testing are used to focus the effort.

stem: Taking the actions needed to meet the test objectives is called what?
explanation: Test control involves the actions necessary to meet the test objectives, using information from test monitoring.

stem: Which is a good testing practice in every SDLC?
explanation: For every development activity there should be a corresponding test activity, so all development work is subject to quality control.
options: Test work for each development activity
Testing starts once all coding has ended
One test level for the whole system

stem: During individual review, what do reviewers log?
explanation: In individual review, each reviewer applies review techniques and logs all anomalies, recommendations and questions they identify.
options: Only the defects confirmed by the author

stem: Which statement about equivalence partitions is true?
explanation: Partitions must not overlap and must be non-empty. They can be valid or invalid and can be found for inputs, outputs, internal values and more, and one test per partition is enough.

stem: Which of these is a conditional branch?
explanation: Conditional branches correspond to decision outcomes: the true or false outcome of an IF, an outcome of a switch/case, or a decision to exit or continue a loop. Straight-line code gives unconditional branches.
options: Choosing to exit or continue a loop
A call to a logging function

stem: Experts estimate alone, discuss any estimates far outside the agreed range, then estimate alone again until they agree. Which technique is this?
explanation: Wideband Delphi is an iterative, expert-based technique: estimates are made in isolation, outliers are discussed, and the process repeats until consensus is reached.

stem: In the qualitative approach to risk assessment, how is the risk level usually found?
explanation: In the qualitative approach the risk level can be determined with a risk matrix. In the quantitative approach it is likelihood multiplied by impact.

stem: A team tests a mobile game and a medical device controller in very different ways. Which principle does this reflect?
explanation: There is no single approach to testing that applies everywhere. Testing is done differently in different contexts, such as a game and a safety-critical device.

stem: In which activity are actual results compared with expected results?
explanation: During test execution, tests are run, actual results are compared with expected results, results are logged and anomalies are analyzed.

stem: When should test analysis and design for a test level begin?
explanation: Test analysis and design for a given test level start during the corresponding development phase, so testing follows the principle of early testing.
options: After that level's code is fully complete

stem: When can the reviewed work product be accepted?
explanation: In fixing and reporting, a defect report is created for each defect so corrective actions can be followed up. Once the exit criteria are reached, the work product can be accepted.
options: Once the exit criteria are reached
As soon as the review meeting ends

stem: Boundary value analysis cannot be applied to which input?
explanation: BVA needs ordered partitions so that boundaries exist. A set of colours has no order, so it has no minimum or maximum.
options: A delivery date in a calendar

stem: How can white-box techniques be used without executing the code?
explanation: White-box techniques can be used in static testing, for example in dry runs of code. They suit code not yet ready to run, pseudocode and other logic that can be shown as a control flow graph.
options: In dry runs during static testing
By checking the user guide wording

stem: Planning Poker is a variant of which estimation technique?
explanation: Planning Poker, common in Agile teams, is a variant of Wideband Delphi in which estimates are made with numbered cards.

stem: A company buys insurance against losses if its booking system fails. Which risk response is this?
explanation: After analysis a risk can be mitigated by testing, accepted, transferred or covered by a contingency plan. Buying insurance moves the risk to another party, which is transfer.

stem: A review finds a defect in a design document. What does debugging involve here?
explanation: Static testing finds defects directly and cannot cause failures, so there is nothing to reproduce or diagnose. Debugging is simply removing the defect.

stem: During which activity are coverage items usually identified?
explanation: Test design often involves identifying coverage items, which guide the test case inputs. Test design also defines test data and test environment requirements.

stem: Which approach derives tests from acceptance criteria as part of system design?
explanation: ATDD derives tests from acceptance criteria during system design, and the tests are written before that part of the application is built.

stem: Which review role decides what is reviewed and provides staff and time?
explanation: The manager decides what is to be reviewed and provides resources such as staff and time. The review leader organizes who is involved and when.

stem: A parcel weight is valid from 1 to 30 kg in whole kilograms. Which value is not a 2-value BVA coverage item for the valid partition?
explanation: 2-value BVA takes each boundary and its closest neighbour in the adjacent partition: 0 and 1 at the lower boundary, 30 and 31 at the upper. 29 is only a 3-value BVA neighbour.

stem: What does performing only black-box testing fail to provide?
explanation: Black-box testing alone gives no measure of code coverage. White-box coverage measures are objective and show where extra tests would raise coverage.
options: Tests derived from the business rules
A measure of actual code coverage

stem: How can a team estimate a very large testing task more accurately?
explanation: Estimates for small tasks are usually more accurate than for large ones, so a large task can be decomposed into smaller tasks that are estimated in turn.

stem: How can product risk analysis results shape testing?
explanation: Product risk analysis results determine test scope, levels and types, techniques and coverage, effort, prioritization, and whether non-testing activities could reduce risk.
options: They remove the need for reviews

stem: Who should preferably carry out confirmation testing after a defect is fixed?
explanation: Confirmation testing is preferably done by the same person who performed the initial test, since they know exactly how the failure appeared.
options: The developer who fixed the defect

stem: How are the main groups of test activities usually carried out?
explanation: Although the activities may look like a logical sequence, they are often implemented iteratively or in parallel and tailored to the system and project.
options: In any order the tester likes
Always in one strict, fixed sequence

stem: Which is a risk or challenge of DevOps for testing?
explanation: DevOps brings challenges: the delivery pipeline must be defined and established, CI/CD tools must be introduced and maintained, and automation needs resources.
options: Feedback on code quality is slower
Test environments become much less stable
The pipeline must be defined and built

stem: Which review role collates anomalies and records decisions made in the review meeting?
explanation: The scribe (recorder) collates anomalies from reviewers and records review information such as decisions and new anomalies found in the meeting.

stem: The rule "if n >= 50" was coded by mistake as "if n = 50". Which value from 3-value BVA would expose the defect?
explanation: At 51 the correct code is true but the faulty code is false, so the test fails. At 49 and 50 both versions agree, which is why 2-value BVA (49 and 50) misses it.

stem: Which knowledge does error guessing draw on?
explanation: Error guessing anticipates errors, defects and failures from how the application worked before, the errors developers tend to make and failures in similar applications.

stem:
Using additional coverage prioritization, test A runs first. Which test runs second?

| Test | Statements covered |
|---|---|
| A | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| B | 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 |
| C | 1, 2, 3, 10 |
| D | 7, 8, 9, 10 |
explanation: After A, test B adds statements 7, 8 and 9 (three new), C adds only 10 (one), and D adds 7, 8, 9 and 10 (four). D gives the highest additional coverage, so it runs second.

stem: What values can risk likelihood take?
explanation: Risk likelihood is the probability of the risk occurring, which is greater than zero and less than one.

stem: How does testing give users indirect representation on a project?
explanation: Testers make sure their understanding of users' needs is considered throughout development. Involving a representative set of real users is usually too costly or impractical.
options: Testers replace all user acceptance tests
Testers keep users' needs in view

stem: Which is a contextual factor that shapes how testing is carried out?
explanation: Contextual factors include stakeholders, team members, business domain (such as criticality and regulations), technical factors, project constraints, organizational factors, the SDLC and tools.
options: The numbering of test case IDs
The font used in test reports

stem: What does shift left usually do to cost and effort?
explanation: Shift left may need extra training, effort and cost early in the process but is expected to save effort and cost later. Stakeholders need to buy into it.

stem: Which review role decides who takes part and when and where the review happens?
explanation: The review leader takes overall responsibility for the review, including who is involved and when and where it takes place.

stem: Using 2-value BVA, a tester identifies four boundary values and the tests exercise three. What is the coverage?
explanation: BVA coverage is boundary values exercised divided by boundary values identified: 3 / 4 = 75%.

stem: When is exploratory testing especially useful?
explanation: Exploratory testing is useful when there are few or inadequate specifications or significant time pressure, and it complements more formal techniques.
options: When coverage must be measured precisely
When a test must be repeatable exactly
When specs are weak or time is short

stem: In requirements-based prioritization, who sets the priorities that order the test cases?
explanation: Requirements-based prioritization orders tests by the priorities of the requirements they trace to, and those requirement priorities are defined by stakeholders.

stem: Which consequence of a product risk does the syllabus name only for extreme cases?
explanation: Product risks can lead to user dissatisfaction, lost revenue and reputation, damage to third parties, high maintenance costs, criminal penalties and, in extreme cases, physical damage, injuries or death.

stem: Which statement about defects and failures is true?
explanation: Some defects fail every time they are executed, others only in specific circumstances, and some never. Failures can also come from environmental conditions, and defects can sit in documents.
options: Every defect fails whenever it is executed
Some defects never cause a failure

stem: A risk register is a work product of which activity?
explanation: Test planning work products include the test plan, test schedule, risk register, and entry and exit criteria. The risk register lists risks with their likelihood, impact and mitigation.

stem: Operations staff test backup, restore and disaster recovery before go-live. Which form of acceptance testing is this?
explanation: Operational acceptance testing checks readiness for operations, such as backup and recovery. User acceptance testing checks fitness for users' business needs.

stem: Which review type is led by a moderator and aims to reach consensus on a technical problem?
explanation: A technical review is done by technically qualified reviewers and led by a moderator. Its objectives include gaining consensus and making decisions on a technical problem.

stem: In a decision table, what does a condition cell marked with a dash (-) mean?
explanation: A dash means the condition's value is irrelevant to the action outcome. N/A marks an infeasible combination, F marks a false condition and a blank action cell means it should not occur.

stem: What usually follows a session of session-based exploratory testing?
explanation: The test session is usually followed by a debriefing between the tester and stakeholders interested in its results. Test session sheets record steps and discoveries.
options: A formal inspection of the charter

stem: A load testing tool is available only on Thursday. How should this affect the test execution schedule?
explanation: The order of test execution must take resource availability into account, such as tools, environments or people available only in a specific time window.
options: Run its tests first, whatever their priority
Run its tests last, after all others
Fit its tests to the tool's free day

stem: Mean time to failure is which kind of test metric?
explanation: Product quality metrics include availability, response time and mean time to failure.

stem: Radiation corrupts the firmware of a satellite, and it stops responding. What does this show?
explanation: Errors and defects are not the only causes of failures. Environmental conditions such as radiation or electromagnetic fields can cause defects in firmware.
options: Static testing would have found it
It was a human error in testing

stem: Which work products typically come from test execution?
explanation: Test execution produces test logs and defect reports. Test cases and charters come from design, test conditions from analysis, and plans from planning.

stem: Component integration testing depends heavily on what?
explanation: Component integration testing covers interfaces and interactions between components and depends heavily on the integration strategy, such as bottom-up, top-down or big-bang.

stem: Which review type follows no defined process and needs no formal output?
explanation: Informal reviews do not follow a defined process or require documented output. Their main objective is detecting anomalies.

stem: How many columns does a full limited-entry decision table have for four independent Boolean conditions?
explanation: Each Boolean condition doubles the combinations: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 16 columns. The number of rules grows exponentially with the number of conditions.

stem: Why should checklists be updated over time?
explanation: Some entries lose effectiveness as developers stop making those errors, and new high-severity defects may need entries, so checklists are updated based on defect analysis.
options: A checklist may hold only ten items

stem: When can running out of time count as an acceptable exit criterion?
explanation: Running out of time or budget can be a valid exit criterion if the stakeholders have reviewed and accepted the risk of going live without further testing.
options: When the product owner sets a date
When the test manager decides to stop
When the planned tests have all run

stem: Which item belongs in a test completion report?
explanation: A test completion report includes a summary, an evaluation against the plan, deviations, impediments, metrics, unmitigated risks and unfixed defects, and lessons learned.

stem: Checking that a system meets users' needs in its operational environment is called what?
explanation: Validation checks that the system meets users' and other stakeholders' needs in its operational environment. Verification checks that it meets the specified requirements.

stem: Stubs, drivers and simulators are created as part of which activity?
explanation: Test environment items such as stubs, drivers, simulators and service virtualizations are test implementation work products.

stem: Which test type derives tests from code, architecture or data flows?
explanation: White-box testing is structure-based: it derives tests from the internal structure or implementation. Black-box testing derives them from specifications.

stem: Which factor raises the level of formality a review needs?
explanation: The required formality depends on the SDLC, process maturity, criticality and complexity of the work product, legal or regulatory requirements and the need for an audit trail.
options: The need for an audit trail

stem:
Ticket rules are shown below. A non-student buys a ticket on a weekday. What result should the test expect?

| Condition or action | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Student | T | T | F | F |
| Weekday | T | F | T | F |
| 50% off | X | | | |
| 20% off | | X | X | |
explanation: Student = F and Weekday = T is rule R3, whose only action marked X is 20% off.

stem: What is the effect of using high-level checklists?
explanation: With high-level checklists some variability in the actual testing is likely, which can give greater coverage but less repeatability.

stem: In Agile development, what are the exit criteria for a releasable item often called?
explanation: Exit criteria that set the team's objective metrics for a releasable item are often called the Definition of Done. Entry criteria for starting work on a story are the Definition of Ready.

stem: Which milestone typically triggers test completion activities?
explanation: Test completion activities occur at milestones such as finishing a test level or an Agile iteration, completing or cancelling a test project, or releasing a system.
options: The first defect found in a sprint
The end of an Agile iteration

stem: How does quality assurance use test results?
explanation: In testing, results are used to fix defects. In QA, they give feedback on how well the development and test processes are performing.
options: As feedback on how processes perform
To decide which of the defects to fix first

stem: At test completion, what is created for defects that are still unresolved?
explanation: For any unresolved defects, change requests or product backlog items are created during test completion.
options: A root cause report for each one

stem: Which statement about test types and test levels is true?
explanation: All four test types can be applied at all test levels, although the focus differs by level. Non-functional testing can even start in reviews or component testing.
options: Each level uses only one type
Each type can be used at any level
White-box tests run only in component test
Non-functional tests run only in system test

skill: FL-3.1.1 Work products for static testing
stem: What must a work product have before static analysis can check it?
explanation: Any work product people can read can be reviewed, but static analysis needs a structure to check against, such as models, code or text with formal syntax.
options: An executable build of the code

stem: What is a key strength of decision table testing?
explanation: Decision tables identify all combinations of conditions systematically and help find gaps or contradictions in the requirements. The number of rules grows exponentially with conditions.
options: It exposes gaps in the requirements
It needs few columns however many conditions

stem: What is the first step in ATDD?
explanation: ATDD starts with a specification workshop where the user story and its acceptance criteria are analyzed, discussed and written, resolving ambiguities. Test cases are created next.

stem: What does a test plan do with respect to the test policy and test strategy?
explanation: A test plan demonstrates that testing will adhere to the existing test policy and test strategy, or explains why it will deviate from them.
options: Defines them for the whole organization

stem: How does configuration management help reproduce earlier test results?
explanation: Configuration management records changed configuration items when a new baseline is created, so the team can revert to a previous baseline to reproduce earlier results.
options: It can revert to a previous baseline
It stores the testers' notes only

stem: When might the whole team approach not be appropriate?
explanation: In some situations, such as safety-critical work, a high level of test independence may be needed, so the whole team approach may not fit.
options: When the team shares one workspace

stem: Besides evaluating coverage, what does good traceability make possible?
explanation: Good traceability helps determine the impact of changes, facilitates audits and helps meet IT governance criteria, as well as supporting coverage evaluation.

stem: Which is a non-functional quality characteristic in ISO/IEC 25010?
explanation: ISO/IEC 25010's non-functional characteristics are performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, maintainability, portability and safety. Functional correctness is a functional aspect.

stem: Which quality characteristic can static testing measure without executing code?
explanation: Static testing can measure characteristics that do not depend on execution, such as maintainability. Dynamic testing measures those that do, such as performance efficiency.

stem: In a state table, what does an empty cell represent?
explanation: Rows are states and columns are events. Unlike a state diagram, a state table shows invalid transitions explicitly, as empty cells.
options: A transition to a final state

stem: An acceptance criterion says: "Orders of 50 items or more get free delivery." Which ATDD test case covers a negative scenario?
explanation: A negative scenario checks behaviour outside the rule: 49 items must not get free delivery. The 50 and 120 item cases are positive, and page speed is a non-functional check the criterion does not mention.
options: An order of 50 items gets free delivery
An order of 120 items gets free delivery
The order page loads in 2 seconds
An order of 49 items is charged delivery

stem: What are the tests in the bottom layer of the test pyramid like?
explanation: Bottom-layer tests are small, isolated and fast, each checking a small piece of functionality, so many of them are needed for reasonable coverage.

stem: A reported anomaly turns out not to be a real defect. What might it be instead?
explanation: Reported anomalies may be real defects or something else, such as a false-positive result or a change request. This is resolved while handling the reports.

stem: Which is a drawback of independent testing?
explanation: Independent testers can be isolated from developers, and developers may lose a sense of responsibility for quality. Independence usually finds different kinds of defects and challenges assumptions.
options: Fewer kinds of defects are found overall

stem: Which activities does the test management role mainly focus on?
explanation: The test management role takes overall responsibility for the test process and focuses on test planning, monitoring, control and completion.

stem: Time is short after a fix. What is the minimum confirmation testing?
explanation: When time or money is short, confirmation testing may be limited to exercising the steps that should reproduce the failure and checking that it no longer occurs.
options: Write new tests covering the whole module
Skip it and rely on regression tests
Rerun the steps that showed the failure

stem: An interface specification lists parameters in a different order from the code calling it. Which testing finds this most cheaply?
explanation: Incorrect interface specifications, such as a mismatched number, type or order of parameters, are among the defects easier and cheaper to find through static testing.

stem: Which coverage criterion guarantees full valid transitions coverage?
explanation: All transitions coverage exercises every valid transition and attempts every invalid one, so it guarantees both valid transitions and all states coverage. All states is the weakest.

stem: A stakeholder cannot say how a user story would be tested. What might this show?
explanation: If a stakeholder does not know how to test a story, it may not be clear enough, may not reflect something valuable to them, or they may just need help testing.
options: The story is not clear enough
The tester should write the code

stem: Component tests and component integration tests, automated in CI, belong to which testing quadrant?
explanation: Q1 is technology facing and supports the team: component and component integration tests that should be automated and run in CI.

stem: In a defect report, what does severity describe?
explanation: Severity is the degree of impact on stakeholders' interests or requirements. Priority to fix is recorded separately.

stem: Which generic tester skill mainly increases the efficiency of testing, for example by using tools?
explanation: Technical knowledge increases efficiency, for example by using appropriate test tools. Domain knowledge helps testers understand and communicate with end users.

stem: Which statement about the two roles in testing is true?
explanation: Different people may take on the roles at different times, and one person can take on both the testing and test management roles at the same time.
options: Agile teams drop the testing role
One person can hold both roles

stem: Why is regression testing a strong candidate for automation?
explanation: Regression suites are run many times and usually grow with each iteration or release, so automating them pays off. Automation should start early.
options: The suites run many times and grow
It always finds the original defect again

stem: Reviews take effort. Why do they usually lower overall project cost?
explanation: Even though reviews can be costly, overall project costs are usually much lower than without them, because less time and effort goes into fixing defects later.
options: They remove the need for testers
They shorten every later test cycle

stem: A transition is labelled "pay [balance > 0] / print receipt". What is "balance > 0"?
explanation: The labelling syntax is event [guard condition] / action. Here pay is the event, balance > 0 the guard and print receipt the action.

stem: Which is a use of acceptance criteria?
explanation: Acceptance criteria define the story's scope, build consensus, describe positive and negative scenarios, serve as the basis for acceptance testing and allow accurate planning and estimation.

stem: Smoke tests and non-functional tests other than usability belong to which testing quadrant?
explanation: Q4 is technology facing and critiques the product: smoke tests and non-functional tests (except usability), which are often automated. Usability is in Q3.

skill: FL-6.2.1 Benefits and risks of automation
stem: Which is a benefit of test automation?
explanation: Benefits include saved time on repetitive work, fewer simple errors, more objective measures, easier access to test information, faster feedback and more time to design deeper tests.
options: No further need for tool maintenance
More time to design deeper tests

stem: Which two activities are part of software testing, as well as running tests? (Choose two.)
explanation: Testing includes static testing such as reviews, and it must be planned, managed, monitored and controlled. Fixing defects is debugging, a non-testing activity.

stem: Which two tasks belong to test implementation? (Choose two.)
explanation: Test implementation creates or acquires testware such as test data, assembles test procedures and suites, and builds and verifies the test environment. Test conditions are defined in analysis.

stem: Which two factors typically set the scope of maintenance testing? (Choose two.)
explanation: The scope of maintenance testing depends on the degree of risk of the change, the size of the existing system and the size of the change.
options: The age of the test tools
The degree of risk of the change

stem: Which two are examples of static analysis tools? (Choose two.)
explanation: Static analysis does not execute the software. Spelling checkers and readability tools are named in the syllabus as static analysis tools; load and coverage tools need execution.

stem: An order can go New to Paid, Paid to Shipped, Shipped to Delivered, New to Cancelled and Paid to Cancelled. Each event sequence starts in New and ends in Delivered or Cancelled. What is the fewest sequences that give 100% valid transitions coverage?
explanation: Each sequence ends in a final state, and Cancelled is reached by two different transitions, so three paths are needed: New-Paid-Shipped-Delivered, New-Cancelled and New-Paid-Cancelled. Two sequences would give all states coverage only.

stem: Which two are examples of rule-oriented acceptance criteria? (Choose two.)
explanation: Rule-oriented criteria include a bullet point verification list or a tabulated input-output mapping. Given/When/Then is the scenario-oriented format.

stem: During release planning, what does a tester typically help with?
explanation: In release planning, testers help write testable user stories and acceptance criteria, join project and quality risk analyses, estimate test effort and plan testing for the release.
options: Writing the code for a story
Approving the budget for each iteration

skill: FL-6.2.1 Benefits and risks of automation
stem: Which two are risks of test automation? (Choose two.)
explanation: Risks include abandoned open-source tools, unrealistic expectations, poor estimates, over-reliance and incompatible tools. Repeatability, speed and easier access to statistics are benefits.
